subject: general
question: In what condition does the body's immune system attack the actual intrinsic factor protein or the cells in your stomach lining that make it?
solution:
The Correct Answer is**Pernicious anaemia.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pernicious anemia **is a condition in which the body can't make enough healthy red blood cells because it lacks **vitamin B12.**
 
• The **immune system **mistakenly attacks the stomach cells that produce intrinsic factor, a protein necessary** for the absorption of vitamin B12.**
 
• Without intrinsic factor, vitamin B12 can't be absorbed and utilized by the body, leading to a deficiency.
 
• This autoimmune response primarily affects the** gastric mucosa**, where the intrinsic factor is produced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
 A neurological disorder typically associated with chronic alcoholism and thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency.
 
 

 2) Hepatic cirrhosis
 A late stage of scarring (fibrosis) of the liver caused by many forms of liver diseases and conditions.
 
 

 4) Hartnup disorder
 A metabolic disorder characterized by impaired absorption of certain amino acids from the diet.
